import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_2/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_2/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_2/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source0 and Source1 on movie_id
join_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the result with Source2 on user_id
# Source2 has columns: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
# We only need age and occupation from Source2 for the target
join_012 = pd.merge(join_01, source2[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Reorder and cast columns to match target schema:
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float]

# Ensure correct dtypes:
join_012['title'] = join_012['title'].astype(str)
join_012['user_id'] = join_012['user_id'].astype(float)
join_012['age'] = join_012['age'].astype(float)
join_012['occupation'] = join_012['occupation'].astype(float)
join_012['movie_id'] = join_012['movie_id'].astype(int)
join_012['rating'] = join_012['rating'].astype(float)
join_012['timestamp'] = join_012['timestamp'].astype(float)

# Select and reorder columns as per target schema
Target3_2 = join_012[['title', 'user_id', 'age', 'occupation', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']]

# Write the final target table to the specified path without the index
Target3_2.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_2_0 and Source3_2_1 on movie_id
join_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', on='movie_id')

# Join the above result with Source3_2_2 on user_id
join_012 = pd.merge(join_01, source2, how='inner', on='user_id')

# Group by the leftmost columns of the target schema (title, user_id, age, occupation, movie_id)
# Aggregate rating and timestamp by average
result = join_012.groupby(
    ['title', 'user_id', 'age', 'occupation', 'movie_id'], as_index=False
).agg({
    'rating': 'mean',
    'timestamp': 'mean'
})

# Ensure column order and names exactly as target schema
result = result[['title', 'user_id', 'age', 'occupation', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']]

# Write to target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
